Endpoint final class

One row in a wishlist directory — a host the user can pick to ssh into. Held as an immutable value object; build via new Endpoint(...) or via Config::load().

Not listed: the methods of SugarCraft\Core\Concerns\Mutable, a trait declared outside src/.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly string $name, public readonly string $host, public readonly int $port = 22, public readonly ?string $user = null, public readonly array $identityFiles = [], public readonly ?string $description = null, public readonly ?string $proxyJump = null, public readonly array $options = [], public readonly array $flags = [], public readonly ?string $remoteCommand = null, public readonly ?string $command = null)
static parsePort(string $host, mixed $raw): intParse+validate a config-supplied port before it reaches the ctor. Accepts ints and unsigned decimal strings only — booleans, floats and anything ((int)) would silently mangle ("notanumber" → 0) are refused by name, not coerced.
toSshArgv(string $binary = 'ssh'): arrayBuild the argv list for ssh(1). The first element is the binary name (ssh); the rest is options, the destination and — per the ssh(1) synopsis ssh [options] destination [command] — an optional remote command riding after the destination. Suitable for pcntl_exec($argv[0], array_slice($argv, 1)).
toTransportArgv(string $binary): arrayBuild the argv list for a custom transport (-027): binary, the -p port leg when it is not 22, the raw flag lane, then the destination — nothing else. The ssh-only machinery (-i/-J/-o legs and the remote-command positional) is left out because mosh-class transports reject it; transportIncompatibles() names what was set but dropped so the launcher can warn instead of silently trimming. The flags lane rides verbatim by design — the user picked a custom binary precisely to speak its dialect.
transportIncompatibles(): arrayThe fixed field names whose values would be silently lost by toTransportArgv() — computed from what is actually set, so a plain mosh row (command: /usr/bin/mosh and nothing else) carries no warning debt.
unsafeOptions(): arrayThe host-key-trust-destruction family (candy-ssh-launcher-029).
displayLine(): stringThe picker row for this endpoint.

Launcher final class

Replaces the current PHP process with ssh(1) connecting to the chosen Endpoint. Uses pcntl_exec() so file descriptors, environment, controlling tty, and exit status all flow through unchanged — the user sees a normal ssh session, including host-key prompts, agent forwarding, and the standard MOTD.

MethodSummary
static firstExecutableSsh(array $candidates = self::SSH_CANDIDATES): ?stringFirst candidate that is an existing executable file, or null when none is — the caller then falls back to DEFAULT_SSH and the honest exit-1 refusal names the default.
setWarningStream($stream): void
__construct(?callable $executor = null)
dispatch(Endpoint $e, string $sshBinary = self::DEFAULT_SSH): voidDispatch into the chosen endpoint. On success, the PHP process is replaced and this method does not return; on failure the executor throws.

Picker class

Tiny terminal picker — renders marker-prefixed display lines (selectedMarker() over displayLine()) of Endpoints. The user moves with ↑/↓, Home/End and PgUp/PgDn (j/k are query letters on every row — the invert model, -060), narrows with type-to-search, and picks with Enter. Returns the selected Endpoint, or null on Esc or the cancel byte (0x03 — what a closed stdin maps to as well). On a real terminal Ctrl-C raises SIGINT, which the picker traps to restore the terminal before exiting 130.

MethodSummary
__construct($in = null, $out = null)
pick(array $endpoints): ?Endpoint
